content.value_statement: Manual release notes are slow and inconsistent. This skill helps configure automated changelogs from commits, pull requests, tags, and release workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains Keep a Changelog sections and semantic versioning rules.
Maps Conventional Commit types to changelog categories.
Provides setup patterns for standard-version, semantic-release, git-cliff, and commitizen.
Includes GitHub Actions workflow examples for automated releases.
Supplies release note templates for public GitHub releases and internal notes.
Lists commit message examples and validation practices.
limitations: Does not run release tools or publish artifacts by itself.
Requires reliable commit history, tags, or pull request metadata.
Examples use placeholder GitHub owner and repository values.
Generated notes still require review for sensitive or internal details.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release Notes
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable changelog format for teams moving from manual notes to structured releases.

use_cases.title: Automate CI Releases
use_cases.description: Configure semantic-release or standard-version workflows that update changelogs during release pipelines.

use_cases.title: Adopt Commit Conventions
use_cases.description: Define commit types, scopes, and validation rules that feed clean changelog sections.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Changelog Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a project without a formal changelog.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to recommend a Keep a Changelog structure for my project. Include sections, version rules, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Map Commit Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for teams adopting commit conventions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to map our commit types to changelog sections. Highlight which types should be hidden from public release notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Release Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup for automated release pipelines.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a release workflow using semantic-release or standard-version. Include required permissions, tokens, and review gates.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing release process.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review our current changelog automation. Identify gaps in commit conventions, CI configuration, sensitive data handling, and release note quality.

output_examples.input: A team wants to stop writing release notes manually.
output: Commit categories mapped to release note sections.
Review checklist for accuracy and sensitive details.

output_examples.input: A project needs fully automated GitHub releases.
output_examples.output: A workflow plan covering release tool setup, token use, changelog files, and release review points.

output_examples.input: Maintainers want cleaner commit messages before release.
output: Commit type rules for features, fixes, performance, and maintenance.
Validation guidance for commitlint or commitizen.

best_practices: Use Conventional Commits consistently before automating release notes.
Review generated changelogs for accuracy, tone, and sensitive information.
Keep release permissions narrow and document each required token.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generated notes without checking customer impact and internal details.
Do not mix unrelated changes in one commit when commits drive changelogs.
Do not reuse placeholder repository URLs or token names without review.

faq.question: Does this skill publish releases automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives patterns and examples for configuring release tools, but execution depends on your environment.

faq.question: Which changelog format does it prefer?
faq.answer: It centers on Keep a Changelog and maps Conventional Commits into clear release sections.

faq.question: Can it work with GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes GitHub Actions examples for semantic-release and manual release workflows.

faq.question: Does it require Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: No. Automation is more reliable when commit messages or pull request labels follow a consistent convention.

faq.question: Can it help with internal release notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes internal note structure for summaries, highlights, breaking changes, known issues, and dependency updates.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use platform secrets, restrict permissions, and review generated notes so tokens or internal details are not exposed.
